etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English ded, deed, from Old English dēad, from Proto-West Germanic *daud, from Proto-Germanic *daudaz. Compare West Frisian dead, dea, Dutch dood, German tot, Danish, Norwegian død, Norwegian Nynorsk daud.

definitions.definition: (usually not comparable) No longer living; deceased. (Also used as a noun.)

quote.citation: 1968, Ray Thomas, "Legend of a Mind", The Moody Blues, In Search of the Lost Chord.
quote.text: Timothy Leary's dead. / No, no no no, he's outside, looking in.

definitions.definition: (usually not comparable) Devoid of living things; barren.

quote.citation: 1886 October – 1887 January, H[enry] Rider Haggard, She: A History of Adventure, London: Longmans, Green, and Co., published 1887, →OCLC:
quote.text: Behold the substance from which all things draw their energy, the bright Spirit of the Globe, without which it cannot live, but must grow cold and dead as the dead moon.

quote.citation: 1913, Arthur Conan Doyle, “(please specify the page)”, in The Poison Belt […], London; New York, N.Y.: Hodder and Stoughton, →OCLC:
quote.text: Was it possible to exist upon a dead world?

definitions.definition: (hyperbolic) Figuratively, not alive; lacking life.

quote.citation: 1600, William Shakespeare, As You Like It, act III, scene 3:
quote.text: When a man's verses cannot be understood, nor a man's good wit seconded with the forward child, understanding, it strikes a man more dead than a great reckoning in a little room.

definitions.definition: (of another person) So hated or offensive as to be absolutely shunned, ignored, or ostracized.

quote.citation: 2020 July 24, Taylor Swift, “My Tears Ricochet”, in Folklore‎[1]:
quote.text: I didn't have it in myself to go with graceAnd you're the hero flying around, saving faceAnd if I'm dead to you, why are you at the wake?

definitions.definition: Doomed; marked for death; as good as dead (literally or as a hyperbole).

quote.citation: 2009, Noel Hynd, Midnight in Madrid‎[2]:
quote.text: You're dead. A million and one thoughts pounded her at once. But one overpowered all the others. This time you're dead.

definitions.definition: Without emotion; impassive.
Stationary; static; immobile or immovable.
Without interest to one of the senses; dull; flat.

quote.citation: 1969 March 31, Kurt Vonnegut, Jr., Slaughterhouse-Five […] (A Seymour Lawrence Book), New York, N.Y.: Delacorte Press, →OCLC, page 65:
quote.text: He stopped, took a swig of the dead champagne. It was like 7-Up.

definitions.definition: Unproductive; fallow.

quote.citation: 2019 April 10, qntm, “CASE HATE RED”, in SCP Foundation‎[3], archived from the original on 29 May 2024:
quote.text: The auditorium opens and the seats fill. As ever, there's a brief, grey dead time while Wheeler waits for all the machinery of the performance to spin up. The anxious feeling is stronger than usual today. It grips him, an uncharacteristic urge to run away. Sure, he thinks. I could just junk my career, right now. Pack it in and make for the stage door. Maybe the taxi'll still be there.

definitions.definition: Past, bygone, vanished.

quote.citation: 1905, Lord Dunsany [i.e., Edward Plunkett, 18th Baron of Dunsany], The Gods of Pegāna, London: [Charles] Elkin Mathews, […], →OCLC, page 40:
quote.text: Then shall the Times that were be Times no more; and it may be that the old, dead days shall return from beyond the Rim, and we who have wept for them shall see those days again, as one who, returning from long travel to his home, comes suddenly on dear, remembered things.

definitions.definition: (of a place) Lacking usual activity; unexpectedly quiet or empty of people.
(not comparable, of a machine, device, or electrical circuit) Completely inactive; currently without power; without a signal; not live.

quote.citation: 1984, William Gibson, chapter 1, in Neuromancer (Sprawl; book 1), New York, N.Y.: Ace Books, →ISBN, page 3:
quote.text: The sky above the port was the color of television, tuned to a dead channel.

quote.citation: 2008, BioWare, Mass Effect, Redwood City: Electronic Arts, →ISBN, →OCLC, PC, scene: Normandy SR-1:
quote.text: Joker: Everything cuts out after that. No comm traffic at all. Just goes dead. There's nothing.

definitions.definition: (of a battery) Unable to emit power, being discharged (flat) or faulty.
(not comparable) Broken or inoperable.
(not comparable) No longer used or required.

quote.citation: 1984, Winston Smock, Technical Writing for Beginners, page 148:
quote.text: No mark of any kind should ever be made on a dead manuscript.

quote.citation: 2017, Zhaomo Yang, Brian Johannesmeyer, Dead Store Elimination (Still) Considered Harmful:
quote.text: In this paper, we survey the set of techniques found in the wild that are intended to prevent data-scrubbing operations from being removed during dead store elimination.

definitions.definition: (engineering) Intentionally designed so as not to impart motion or power.
(not comparable, sports) Not in play.
(not comparable, golf, of a golf ball) Lying so near the hole that the player is certain to hole it in the next stroke.
(not comparable, baseball, slang, 1800s) Tagged out.
(not comparable) Full and complete (usually applied to nouns involving lack of motion, sound, activity, or other signs of life).
(not comparable) Exact; on the dot.
Experiencing pins and needles (paresthesia).
(hyperbolic) Dying of laughter.

quote.citation: 2023 March 3, ihatethis6666666, “I am dead ☠️”, in Reddit‎[4], r/vanderpumprules:
quote.text: Lmao I’m dead this was me to my fiancé since I found out in the car and my son was in the back seat 😭

definitions.definition: Expresses shock, second-hand embarrassment, etc.
(text messaging or Internet slang, sometimes as a standalone word, often with 💀) Expresses an emotional reaction associated with hyperbolic senses of die:
(acoustics) Constructed so as not to reflect or transmit sound; soundless; anechoic.
(obsolete) Bringing death; deadly.

quote.citation: c. 1596 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Life and Death of King Iohn”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act V, scene vii]:
quote.text: You breathe these dead news in as dead an ear.

definitions.definition: (law) Cut off from the rights of a citizen; deprived of the power of enjoying the rights of property.
(rare, especially religion, often with "to") Indifferent to; having no obligation toward; no longer subject to or ruled by (sin, guilt, pleasure, etc).

quote.citation: 1839, William Jenks, The Comprehensive Commentary on the Holy Bible: Acts-Revelation, page 361:
quote.text: He was dead to the law. Whatever account others might make of it, yet, for his part, he was dead to it.  […]  But though he was thus dead to the law, yet he  […]  was far from thinking himself discharged from his duty to God' on the contrary, he was dead to the law, that he might live unto God.

quote.citation: 1849, Robert Haldane, Exposition of the Epistle to the Romans, page 255:
quote.text: But he died to the guilt of sin—to the guilt of his people's sins which he had taken upon him; and they, dying with him, as is above declared, die to sin precisely in the same sense in which he died to it.  […]  He was not justified from it till his resurrection, but from that moment he was dead to it. When he shall appear the second time, it will be "without sin."

definitions.definition: (linguistics) Of a syllable in languages such as Thai and Burmese: ending abruptly.

quote.citation: 2011, Russ Crowley, Learning Thai, Your Great Adventure, page 28:
quote.text: […]  syllable is dead, the tone will depend on whether the vowel is short or long.

definitions.definition: (degree, informal, colloquial) Exactly.

quote.citation: 2003 December 1, Brian Long, RX-7 Mazda’s Rotary Engine Sports Car: Updated & Enlarged Edition, Veloce Publishing Ltd, →ISBN, page 145:
quote.text: Independent tests later confirmed [the figures] to be accurate, with Car & Driver seeing 159mph (254kph), 0.60 in five seconds dead, and an amazingly high 0.97g.

quote.citation: 2023 November 29, Peter Plisner, “The winds of change in Catesby Tunnel”, in RAIL, number 997, page 56:
quote.text: And because the tunnel is dead straight, it's perfect for reaching high speeds.

definitions.definition: (degree, informal, colloquial) Very, absolutely, extremely.

quote.citation: 1899 February, Joseph Conrad, “The Heart of Darkness”, in Blackwood’s Edinburgh Magazine, volume CLXV, number M, New York, N.Y.: The Leonard Scott Publishing Company, […], →OCLC, part I, page 216:
quote.text: I knew once a Scotch sailmaker who was certain, dead sure, there were people in Mars.

definitions.definition: Suddenly and completely.
(informal) As if dead.

quote.citation: 1849 May – 1850 November, Charles Dickens, chapter 2, in The Personal History of David Copperfield, London: Bradbury & Evans, […], published 1850, →OCLC:
quote.text: I was tired of reading, and dead sleepy.

definitions.definition: (often with "the") Time when coldness, darkness, or stillness is most intense.
(with "the") Those who have died: dead people.
(transitive) To prevent by disabling; to stop.

quote.citation: 1826, The Whole Works of the Right Rev. Edward Reynolds, Lord Bishop of Norwich, collected by Edward Reynolds, Benedict Riveley, and Alexander Chalmers. pp. 227. London: B. Holdsworth.
quote.text: “What a man should do, when finds his natural impotency dead him in spiritual works”

definitions.definition: (transitive) To make dead; to deaden; to deprive of life, force, or vigour.

quote.citation: 1614–1615, Homer, “(please specify the book number)”, in Geo[rge] Chapman, transl., Homer’s Odysses. […], London:  […]  Rich[ard] Field [and William Jaggard], for Nathaniell Butter, published 1615, →OCLC; republished in The Odysseys of Homer, […], volume (please specify the book number), London: John Russell Smith, […], 1857, →OCLC:
quote.text: Heaven's stern decree, / With many an ill, hath numb'd and deaded me.The spelling has been modernized.

definitions.definition: (transitive, UK, US, slang) To kill.

quote.text: TOMMY:”Honestly, I’d love to help you with that but I’ve got a surplus of motherfuckers that I need to dead right now.”

definitions.definition: (transitive, African-American Vernacular, slang, by extension) To discontinue or put an end to (something).

quote.text: "Shorty, whatchu got in your pocket? Let me see that hat." ¶ "Nah, man. Dead that." Out would come the .32. ¶ "Oh, aight. You got that, shorty, you got that."
